# Issue #56: Quick reference

**What it does:** "Grid" is the first item in **More tools**. Picking it, or pressing **G**, opens a left-side panel with **Show grid** and **Snap to grid** switches. The grid toggles were removed from **Preferences**.

## Changes by chain

1. **Panel state and open logic** in [GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx)
   - [L21](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L21) `isGridPanelOpenAtom`: open/closed flag. It's a jotai atom, kept out of app state so it isn't saved or added to snapshots.
   - [L27](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L27) `openGridPanel()`: switches to the selection tool, clears the selection and opens the panel. The menu item and the G key both use it.

2. **Panel component** in [GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx) and [GridPanel.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.scss)
   - [L91](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L91), [L99](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L99): the switches run the existing grid actions.
   - [L51](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L51) `shouldClose`: closes the panel on a tool change, or when the element properties panel would appear.
   - [L69](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L69): Escape closes the panel.
   - [L75](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L75): hidden in view mode, and when a host app sets the `gridModeEnabled` prop.

3. **Toolbar item** in [Toolbar.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx)
   - [L124-130](packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx#L124-L130): Grid item with a "G" hint; it doesn't turn the grid on.
   - [L89](packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx#L89), [L105](packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx#L105): More tools turns blue and shows the grid icon while the panel is open.

4. **Placement** in [LayerUI.tsx:305](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx#L305): the panel sits in the left column, above the properties panel.

5. **G shortcut** in [App.tsx:5575](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L5575)
   - It only works with no modifier held.
   - It's skipped when the background picker applies (a fillable tool or selection is active), so that G keeps opening the picker.
   - Shift+G, Ctrl+G and Ctrl+Shift+G are unchanged.

6. **Preferences cleanup** in [DefaultItems.tsx:638](packages/excalidraw/components/main-menu/DefaultItems.tsx#L638)
   - The grid items are removed from the default list.
   - The public `Preferences.ToggleGridMode` and `Preferences.ToggleGridSnapMode` exports are kept.
   - The right-click menu and `Ctrl+'` are unchanged.

7. **Labels** in [en.json](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json): `toolBar.grid` ([L359](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json#L359)) and `labels.showGrid` ([L118](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json#L118)).

## Status

- All 1,690 tests pass; typecheck, lint and Prettier are clean.
- No tests were added or modified.

## Follow-ups

- **Tests (separate chat):** use `handleKeyboardGlobally={true}` for key tests, and stub `ResizeObserver` for tests that open the background picker.
- **Optional:** add a Help dialog entry for G, and add the Grid item to the mobile toolbar.

```text
import { useEffect } from "react";

import { EVENT, KEYS, isSelectionLikeTool } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { showSelectedShapeActions } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { NonDeletedExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { actionToggleGridMode, actionToggleGridSnapMode } from "../actions";
import { atom, useAtom } from "../editor-jotai";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { useExcalidrawActionManager } from "./App";
import { Island } from "./Island";
import { Switch } from "./Switch";

import "./GridPanel.scss";

import type { AppClassProperties, UIAppState } from "../types";

/** whether the grid settings panel (opened from the extra-tools menu) is open */
export const isGridPanelOpenAtom = atom(false);

/**
 * Opens the grid panel like picking a tool: switches to the selection tool
 * and clears the selection so no other tool or properties panel stays active.
 */
export const openGridPanel = (app: AppClassProperties) => {
  app.setActiveTool({ type: app.state.preferredSelectionTool.type });
  app.setAppState({ selectedElementIds: {}, selectedGroupIds: {} });
  app.updateEditorAtom(isGridPanelOpenAtom, true);
};

/**
 * Left-side panel with the grid toggles, shown after picking "Grid" in the
 * extra-tools menu (like the properties panel shown for the frame tool).
 * Closes when the user switches to another tool, selects or edits elements
 * (anything that brings up the properties panel), or presses Escape.
 */
export const GridPanel = ({
  appState,
  elements,
}: {
  appState: UIAppState;
  elements: readonly NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[];
}) => {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useAtom(isGridPanelOpenAtom);
  const actionManager = useExcalidrawActionManager();

  // opening the panel switches to the selection tool and clears the
  // selection, so this only becomes true once the user moves on
  const shouldClose =
    !isSelectionLikeTool(appState.activeTool.type) ||
    showSelectedShapeActions(appState, elements);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (shouldClose) {
      setIsOpen(false);
    }
  }, [shouldClose, setIsOpen]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isOpen) {
      return;
    }
    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === KEYS.ESCAPE) {
        setIsOpen(false);
      }
    };
    document.addEventListener(EVENT.KEYDOWN, onKeyDown);
    return () => document.removeEventListener(EVENT.KEYDOWN, onKeyDown);
  }, [isOpen, setIsOpen]);

  if (
    !isOpen ||
    shouldClose ||
    appState.viewModeEnabled ||
    !actionManager.isActionEnabled(actionToggleGridMode)
  ) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <Island className="GridPanel" padding={2} data-viewport-ui="side">
      <fieldset>
        <legend>{t("toolBar.grid")}</legend>
        <GridPanelToggle
          name="grid-panel-show-grid"
          label={t("labels.showGrid")}
          checked={appState.gridModeEnabled}
          onChange={() =>
            actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleGridMode, "ui")
          }
        />
        <GridPanelToggle
          name="grid-panel-snap-to-grid"
          label={t("labels.toggleGridSnap")}
          checked={appState.gridSnapEnabled}
          onChange={() =>
            actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleGridSnapMode, "ui")
          }
        />
      </fieldset>
    </Island>
  );
};

const GridPanelToggle = ({
  name,
  label,
  checked,
  onChange,
}: {
  name: string;
  label: string;
  checked: boolean;
  onChange: () => void;
}) => (
  <div className="GridPanel__toggle">
    <label htmlFor={name}>{label}</label>
    <Switch name={name} title={label} checked={checked} onChange={onChange} />
  </div>
);
```

```text
import { queryByText, queryByTestId } from "@testing-library/react";
import { useMemo } from "react";

      expect(
        container.getElementsByClassName("disable-zen-mode--visible").length,
      ).toBe(0);
      fireEvent.contextMenu(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, {
        button: 2,
        clientX: 1,
        clientY: 1,
      });
      const contextMenu = document.querySelector(".context-menu");
      expect(queryByText(contextMenu as HTMLElement, "Show grid")).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe("Test grid visibility and grid snapping are independent", () => {

      await render(<Excalidraw />);
      API.setAppState({ objectsSnapModeEnabled: true });

      act(() => {

      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(h.state.objectsSnapModeEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("toggling grid snapping should not show the grid", async () => {
      await render(<Excalidraw />);

      act(() => {
        h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleGridSnapMode);
      });
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(h.state.gridSize);
```

```text
export type KeyboardModifiers = {
  alt?: boolean;
  shift?: boolean;
  ctrl?: boolean;
};
export class Keyboard {
  static withModifierKeys = (modifiers: KeyboardModifiers, cb: () => void) => {
    const prevAltKey = altKey;
    const prevShiftKey = shiftKey;
    const prevCtrlKey = ctrlKey;

    altKey = !!modifiers.alt;
    shiftKey = !!modifiers.shift;
    ctrlKey = !!modifiers.ctrl;

    try {
      cb();
    } finally {
      altKey = prevAltKey;
      shiftKey = prevShiftKey;
      ctrlKey = prevCtrlKey;
    }
  };

  static keyDown = (
    key: string,
    target: HTMLElement | Document | Window = document,
  ) => {
    fireEvent.keyDown(target, {
      key,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };

  static keyUp = (
    key: string,
    target: HTMLElement | Document | Window = document,
  ) => {
    fireEvent.keyUp(target, {
      key,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };

  static keyPress = (key: string, target?: HTMLElement | Document | Window) => {
    Keyboard.keyDown(key, target);
    Keyboard.keyUp(key, target);
  };

  static codeDown = (code: string) => {
    fireEvent.keyDown(document, {
      code,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };
```

```text
import React from "react";

import { DropdownMenu as DropdownMenuPrimitive } from "radix-ui";

import { CLASSES } from "@excalidraw/common";

import DropdownMenuContent from "./DropdownMenuContent";
import DropdownMenuGroup from "./DropdownMenuGroup";
import DropdownMenuItem from "./DropdownMenuItem";
import DropdownMenuItemCustom from "./DropdownMenuItemCustom";
import DropdownMenuItemLink from "./DropdownMenuItemLink";
import MenuSeparator from "./DropdownMenuSeparator";
import DropdownMenuSub from "./DropdownMenuSub";
import DropdownMenuTrigger from "./DropdownMenuTrigger";
import DropdownMenuItemCheckbox from "./DropdownMenuItemCheckbox";
import {
  getMenuContentComponent,
  getMenuTriggerComponent,
} from "./dropdownMenuUtils";

import "./DropdownMenu.scss";

const DropdownMenu = ({
  children,
  open,
}: {
  children?: React.ReactNode;
  open: boolean;
}) => {
  const MenuTriggerComp = getMenuTriggerComponent(children);
  const MenuContentComp = getMenuContentComponent(children);
  const MenuContentWithState =
    MenuContentComp && React.isValidElement(MenuContentComp)
      ? React.cloneElement(
          MenuContentComp as React.ReactElement<
            React.ComponentProps<typeof DropdownMenuContent>
          >,
          { open },
        )
      : MenuContentComp;

  return (
    <DropdownMenuPrimitive.Root open={open} modal={false}>
      <div
        className={CLASSES.DROPDOWN_MENU_EVENT_WRAPPER}
        style={{
          // remove this div from box layout
          display: "contents",
        }}
      >
        {MenuTriggerComp}
        {MenuContentWithState}
      </div>
    </DropdownMenuPrimitive.Root>
  );
};

DropdownMenu.Trigger = DropdownMenuTrigger;
DropdownMenu.Content = DropdownMenuContent;
DropdownMenu.Item = DropdownMenuItem;
DropdownMenu.ItemCheckbox = DropdownMenuItemCheckbox;
DropdownMenu.ItemLink = DropdownMenuItemLink;
DropdownMenu.ItemCustom = DropdownMenuItemCustom;
DropdownMenu.Group = DropdownMenuGroup;
DropdownMenu.Separator = MenuSeparator;
DropdownMenu.Sub = DropdownMenuSub;
import clsx from "clsx";

import { DropdownMenu as DropdownMenuPrimitive } from "radix-ui";

import { useEditorInterface } from "../App";

const MenuTrigger = ({
  className = "",
  children,
  onToggle,
  title,
  ...rest
}: {
  className?: string;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  onToggle: () => void;
  title?: string;
} & Omit<React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "onSelect">) => {
  const editorInterface = useEditorInterface();
  const classNames = clsx(
    `dropdown-menu-button ${className}`,
    "zen-mode-transition",
    {
      "dropdown-menu-button--mobile": editorInterface.formFactor === "phone",
    },
  ).trim();
  return (
    <DropdownMenuPrimitive.Trigger
      className={classNames}
      onClick={onToggle}
      type="button"
      data-testid="dropdown-menu-button"
      title={title}
      {...rest}
    >
      {children}
    </DropdownMenuPrimitive.Trigger>
  );
};

export default MenuTrigger;
MenuTrigger.displayName = "DropdownMenuTrigger";
```

```typescript
    ".App-toolbar__extra-tools-dropdown",

  document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>(`input[name="${name}"]`)!;

const stubResizeObserver = () => {

  (global as any).ResizeObserver = class ResizeObserver {
    observe() {}
    unobserve() {}
    disconnect() {}
  };
};

      API.setElements([rectangle]);
      API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);

      expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("rectangle");

      pickGridFromExtraTools();

      expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("selection");
      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({});
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should highlight More tools while the panel is open", () => {
      expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).not.toHaveClass(
        "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
      );

      pickGridFromExtraTools();
      expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).toHaveClass(
        "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
      );

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
      expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).not.toHaveClass(
        "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
      );
    });
  });

  describe("panel", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
      pickGridFromExtraTools();
    });

    it("should toggle grid visibility from the Show grid switch", () => {
      const showGrid = getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid");
      expect(showGrid.checked).toBe(false);

      fireEvent.click(showGrid);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);

      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid"));
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("should toggle grid snapping from the Snap to grid switch", () => {
      const snapToGrid = getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid");
      expect(snapToGrid.checked).toBe(false);

      fireEvent.click(snapToGrid);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").checked).toBe(true);

      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid"));
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("should reflect grid state changed elsewhere", () => {
      API.setAppState({ gridModeEnabled: true, gridSnapEnabled: true });

      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").checked).toBe(true);
    });

    it("should stay open after toggling a switch", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid"));
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid"));
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should close on Escape", () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should close when switching to another tool", () => {
      UI.clickTool("rectangle");
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

      // and stay closed when coming back to the selection tool
      UI.clickTool("selection");
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should close when an element gets selected", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);
      act(() => {
        API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
      });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

      // and stay closed after deselecting
      act(() => {
        API.clearSelection();
      });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should be hidden in view mode", () => {
      API.setAppState({ viewModeEnabled: true });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });
  });

  describe("G shortcut", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      stubResizeObserver();
      await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    });

    it("should toggle the panel with the selection tool and nothing selected", () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should keep opening the background picker for fillable tools", () => {
      UI.clickTool("rectangle");

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);

      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.openPopup).toBe("elementBackground");
      expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("rectangle");
    });

    it("should keep opening the background picker for selected fillable elements", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);
      act(() => {
        API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
      });

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);

      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.openPopup).toBe("elementBackground");
      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [rectangle.id]: true });
    });

    it.each([
      ["Shift", { shift: true }],
      ["Alt", { alt: true }],
      ["Ctrl", { ctrl: true }],
      ["Ctrl+Shift", { ctrl: true, shift: true }],
    ])("should not open the panel with %s held", (_, modifiers) => {
      Keyboard.withModifierKeys(modifiers, () => {
        Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should still group elements with Ctrl+G", () => {
      const rect1 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0 });
      const rect2 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 100 });
      API.setElements([rect1, rect2]);
      act(() => {
        API.setSelectedElements([rect1, rect2]);
      });

      Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
        Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      });

      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.elements[0].groupIds).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(h.elements[0].groupIds).toEqual(h.elements[1].groupIds);
    });

    it("should not open the panel in view mode", () => {
      API.setAppState({ viewModeEnabled: true });
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });
  });

  describe("gridModeEnabled prop", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      await render(
        <Excalidraw gridModeEnabled={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />,
      );
    });

    it("should hide the Grid item in More tools", () => {
      const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
      expect(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")).toBe(null);
      // the rest of the menu still renders
      expect(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-frame")).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should ignore the G shortcut", () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
    });
  });
});

describe("Preferences menu", () => {
  const openPreferences = (container: HTMLElement) => {
    fireEvent.click(container.querySelector(".dropdown-menu-button")!);
    const trigger = queryByText(
      document.querySelector(".dropdown-menu") as HTMLElement,
      "Preferences",
    )!.closest("[role='menuitem']")!;
    fireEvent.keyDown(trigger, { key: "ArrowRight" });
    return document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
      ".excalidraw-main-menu-preferences-submenu",
    )!;
  };

  it("should no longer list the grid toggles by default", async () => {
    const { container } = await render(<Excalidraw />);
    const submenu = openPreferences(container);

    expect(submenu).not.toBe(null);
    // sanity check that the submenu contents rendered
    expect(queryByText(submenu, "Zen mode")).not.toBe(null);
    expect(queryByText(submenu, "Toggle grid")).toBe(null);
    expect(queryByText(submenu, "Snap to grid")).toBe(null);
  });

  it("should still allow hosts to add the grid toggles explicitly", async () => {
    const { container } = await render(
      <Excalidraw>
        <MainMenu>
          <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences>
            <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.ToggleGridMode />
            <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.ToggleGridSnapMode />
          </MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences>
        </MainMenu>
      </Excalidraw>,
    );
    const submenu = openPreferences(container);

    expect(queryByText(submenu, "Toggle grid")).not.toBe(null);
    expect(queryByText(submenu, "Snap to grid")).not.toBe(null);
  });
});

describe("context menu grid toggle", () => {
  it("should not open the grid panel", async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw />);
    fireEvent.contextMenu(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, {
      button: 2,
      clientX: 1,
      clientY: 1,
    });
    const contextMenu = document.querySelector(".context-menu");
    fireEvent.click(queryByText(contextMenu as HTMLElement, "Toggle grid")!);

    expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
    expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
  });
});
```

I added 26 tests for the grid toolbar in a new file, [gridPanel.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx), and fixed one existing test. The full suite passes (1,716 tests), and typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean. Nothing is committed.

**What the new tests cover:**
- **More tools item:** Grid is the first item and shows a "G" hint. Picking it opens the panel without turning the grid on, switches to the selection tool, and clears the selection. More tools is highlighted while the panel is open and goes back to normal after Escape.
- **Panel:**
  - The Show grid and Snap to grid switches each toggle their setting and leave the other one alone.
  - The switches update when the grid settings are changed elsewhere, and the panel stays open after a switch is toggled.
  - The panel closes on Escape, on a tool change and when an element is selected, and stays closed afterwards. It is hidden in view mode.
- **G shortcut:**
  - G opens and closes the panel when the selection tool is active and nothing is selected.
  - G still opens the background picker when a fillable tool is active or a fillable element is selected.
  - Shift, Alt, Ctrl and Ctrl+Shift with G don't open the panel, Ctrl+G still groups, and G does nothing in view mode.
- **`gridModeEnabled` prop:** when a host app sets it, the Grid item is hidden and G is ignored.
- **Preferences:** the default submenu no longer lists the grid toggles. A host app can still add them with `Preferences.ToggleGridMode` and `Preferences.ToggleGridSnapMode`.
- **Right-click menu:** "Toggle grid" still works and doesn't open the panel.

**Existing test fixed:** [excalidraw.test.tsx:154](packages/excalidraw/tests/excalidraw.test.tsx#L154) checked that "Show grid" was missing from the right-click menu. That item has always been labelled "Toggle grid", so the check passed no matter what. Since "Show grid" is now a real label, I changed it to check for "Toggle grid".

**Two things I found while writing the tests:**
1. **The panel's open/closed flag is shared and survives a reload of the editor.** It lives in a store shared by every Excalidraw instance on the page, and it isn't reset when the editor unmounts. The tests reset it before each run. In a real host app, if Excalidraw unmounts with the panel open and then remounts, the panel comes back open. Other panels that use the same store behave the same way, so this may be acceptable, but you should decide that on purpose.
2. **The `gridModeEnabled={true}` prop doesn't turn the grid on.** In the tests, the grid stays off after load. This isn't caused by your changes, but it means the "G is ignored" test only checks that the grid setting doesn't change, not that it stays on.

```tsx
const openExtraToolsMenu = () => {
  fireEvent.click(getExtraToolsTrigger());
  return document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
    ".App-toolbar__extra-tools-dropdown",
  )!;
};

const pickGridFromExtraTools = () => {
  const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
  fireEvent.click(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")!);
};

const getSwitch = (name: string) =>
  document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>(`input[name="${name}"]`)!;

const stubResizeObserver = () => {
  // radix popovers (e.g. the background color picker) need ResizeObserver
  (global as any).ResizeObserver = class ResizeObserver {
    observe() {}
    unobserve() {}
    disconnect() {}
  };
};

beforeEach(() => {
  // the editor jotai store is module-level, so reset the panel between tests
  editorJotaiStore.set(isGridPanelOpenAtom, false);
});
```

- **Helpers:** each one uses a class name or `data-testid` from your code: `.GridPanel`, `toolbar-grid`, and the switch names `grid-panel-show-grid` and `grid-panel-snap-to-grid`. If one of those is renamed, the tests fail loudly instead of passing quietly.
- **`stubResizeObserver`:** this is a copy of what `togglePopover` in [test-utils.ts:238](packages/excalidraw/tests/test-utils.ts#L238) does. The test environment has no `ResizeObserver`, and the background color picker needs one. Your summary's follow-up note flagged this.
- **The top-level `beforeEach`:** I added it after the first run, when 5 tests failed. The panel's open flag (`isGridPanelOpenAtom`) lives in a store shared by the whole module, so it carried over from one test to the next. For example, a panel left open by one test made the next test's first G press close it instead of opening it. Without this reset, results would depend on the order the tests run in.

## 1. More tools menu item ([L50-L106](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx#L50-L106))

These cover change #3 (the toolbar item), which had no tests. Every test in this group renders `<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />`. The flag makes key presses on `document` reach the editor, as in [contextmenu.test.tsx:65](packages/excalidraw/tests/contextmenu.test.tsx#L65).

### 1a. First item, with a "G" hint

```tsx
it("should be the first item in More tools, with a G shortcut", () => {
  const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
  const items = menu.querySelectorAll(".dropdown-menu-item");
  const gridItem = queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")!;

  expect(items[0]).toBe(gridItem);
  expect(gridItem.textContent).toContain("Grid");
  expect(
    gridItem.querySelector(".dropdown-menu-item__shortcut")?.textContent,
  ).toBe("G");
});
```

- **Checks:** Grid is the first item, its label comes from `toolBar.grid` in `en.json`, and its hint reads "G".
- **Why:** "first item in More tools" is in the issue requirements. Someone could later add an item above it, or a missing translation key could show the raw key instead of "Grid". This test catches both.

### 1b. Opens the panel without turning the grid on

```tsx
it("should open the panel without turning the grid on", () => {
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

  pickGridFromExtraTools();

  expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
  expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
  expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
});
```

- **Checks:** picking Grid shows the panel and leaves both grid settings off.
- **Why:** the summary says the item "doesn't turn the grid on". Without this test, a later change could make the item run `actionToggleGridMode` directly, the way the right-click item does, and nothing would catch it.

### 1c. Switches to the selection tool and clears the selection

```tsx
it("should switch to the selection tool and clear the selection", () => {
  const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
  API.setElements([rectangle]);
  API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
  UI.clickTool("rectangle");
  expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("rectangle");

  pickGridFromExtraTools();

  expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("selection");
  expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({});
  expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
});
```

- **Checks:** `openGridPanel()` ([GridPanel.tsx:27](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L27)) resets the tool and the selection.
- **Why:** this is the most fragile part of the design. The panel closes itself whenever a non-selection tool is active or the properties panel would show (`shouldClose`). If `openGridPanel` stopped resetting either one, the panel would open and close straight away, and the user would see nothing. The last line checks that the panel is still visible after the reset.

### 1d. More tools is highlighted while the panel is open

```tsx
it("should highlight More tools while the panel is open", () => {
  expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).not.toHaveClass(
    "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
  );

  pickGridFromExtraTools();
  expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).toHaveClass(
    "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
  );

  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
  expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).not.toHaveClass(
    "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
  );
});
```

- **Checks:** the `isGridPanelOpen ||` clause added at [Toolbar.tsx:89](packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx#L89) turns the button blue, and the highlight goes away when the panel closes.
- **Why:** this test exposed the shared-store problem. Before the reset was added, the button was already blue at the first check, because an earlier test had left the panel open.

## 2. The panel itself ([L108-L184](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx#L108-L184))

These cover change #2. Every test here starts with the panel open (`pickGridFromExtraTools()` in `beforeEach`).

### 2a and 2b. Each switch toggles one setting and leaves the other alone

```tsx
it("should toggle grid visibility from the Show grid switch", () => {
  const showGrid = getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid");
  expect(showGrid.checked).toBe(false);

  fireEvent.click(showGrid);
  expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
  expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
  expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);

  fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid"));
  expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
});

it("should toggle grid snapping from the Snap to grid switch", () => {
  const snapToGrid = getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid");
  expect(snapToGrid.checked).toBe(false);

  fireEvent.click(snapToGrid);
  expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(true);
  expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
  expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").checked).toBe(true);

  fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid"));
  expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
});
```

- **Checks:** each switch toggles its own setting both on and off, and leaves the other one alone. The on-screen switch also updates.
- **Why:** the old tests in [excalidraw.test.tsx:159-182](packages/excalidraw/tests/excalidraw.test.tsx#L159-L182) ("grid visibility and grid snapping are independent") call `executeAction` directly. These two do the same checks through the actual UI, so they would catch the two switches' `onChange` handlers being swapped. The second click covers the "off" direction.

### 2c. The switches follow changes made elsewhere

```tsx
it("should reflect grid state changed elsewhere", () => {
  API.setAppState({ gridModeEnabled: true, gridSnapEnabled: true });

  expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);
  expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").checked).toBe(true);
});
```

- **Why:** the grid can still be toggled from other places: `Ctrl+'`, the right-click menu, or a host app. The switches have to read app state rather than keep their own copy, or they go out of sync.

### 2d. The panel stays open after toggling

```tsx
it("should stay open after toggling a switch", () => {
  fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid"));
  fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid"));
  expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** toggling a grid action updates app state, and `shouldClose` is recalculated from app state. This makes sure a toggle doesn't accidentally meet a close condition.

### 2e. Escape closes the panel

```tsx
it("should close on Escape", () => {
  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** this covers the `keydown` listener at [GridPanel.tsx:69](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L69). It's the only way to close the panel without changing the tool or the selection.

### 2f. Switching tools closes it, and coming back doesn't reopen it

```tsx
it("should close when switching to another tool", () => {
  UI.clickTool("rectangle");
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

  // and stay closed when coming back to the selection tool
  UI.clickTool("selection");
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** the second half matters most. The render check `!isOpen || shouldClose` would hide the panel while the rectangle tool is active even if the flag were never cleared. In that case, switching back to the selection tool would make the panel reappear. This proves the `useEffect` really sets the flag to false.

### 2g. Selecting an element closes it, and deselecting doesn't reopen it

```tsx
it("should close when an element gets selected", () => {
  const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
  API.setElements([rectangle]);
  act(() => {
    API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
  });
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

  // and stay closed after deselecting
  API.setAppState({ selectedElementIds: {} });
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** this covers the `showSelectedShapeActions` part of `shouldClose`, so the grid panel and the properties panel never show at the same time. It also checks that the panel stays closed after deselecting, for the same reason as 2f.
- **Note:** I first used `API.clearSelection()` here, but its built-in check failed in this setup, so the test sets the selection to empty directly.

### 2h. Hidden in view mode

```tsx
it("should be hidden in view mode", () => {
  API.setAppState({ viewModeEnabled: true });
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** this covers the `appState.viewModeEnabled` check at [GridPanel.tsx:75](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L75). View mode is read-only, so grid settings shouldn't be offered.

## 3. The G shortcut ([L186-L259](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx#L186-L259))

These cover change #5, which is the riskiest change because G already did something. Many existing tests press G: [regressionTests.test.tsx:481](packages/excalidraw/tests/regressionTests.test.tsx#L481), [:530](packages/excalidraw/tests/regressionTests.test.tsx#L530), [contextmenu.test.tsx:268](packages/excalidraw/tests/contextmenu.test.tsx#L268) and others. Almost all of those press **Ctrl+G** to group. No existing test checked plain G opening the background picker, so the new handler could have broken it without any test failing.

### 3a. G opens and closes the panel

```tsx
it("should toggle the panel with the selection tool and nothing selected", () => {
  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
  expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
  expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);

  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** this is the main way the shortcut works. It covers both branches of the `if (editorJotaiStore.get(isGridPanelOpenAtom))` at [App.tsx:5589](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L5589). It also checks that G only opens the panel and doesn't turn the grid on.

### 3b and 3c. G still opens the background picker

```tsx
it("should keep opening the background picker for fillable tools", () => {
  UI.clickTool("rectangle");

  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);

  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
  expect(h.state.openPopup).toBe("elementBackground");
  expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("rectangle");
});

it("should keep opening the background picker for selected fillable elements", () => {
  const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
  API.setElements([rectangle]);
  act(() => {
    API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
  });

  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);

  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
  expect(h.state.openPopup).toBe("elementBackground");
  expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [rectangle.id]: true });
});
```

- **Why:** these are the regression tests for the two `hasBackground` checks in the new handler, one for the active tool and one for selected elements. Without them, a tidy-up that removes either check would quietly take G away from the color picker. The last line of each test also checks that `openGridPanel` didn't run, because it would have switched the tool or cleared the selection.
- **Note:** these are the tests that need `stubResizeObserver()`, because opening the picker renders a popover.

### 3d. G with a modifier key does nothing (one test run 4 times)

```tsx
it.each([
  ["Shift", { shift: true }],
  ["Alt", { alt: true }],
  ["Ctrl", { ctrl: true }],
  ["Ctrl+Shift", { ctrl: true, shift: true }],
])("should not open the panel with %s held", (_, modifiers) => {
  Keyboard.withModifierKeys(modifiers, () => {
    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
  });
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** this covers the `!event.shiftKey && !event.altKey && !event.ctrlKey && !event.metaKey` checks. Each modifier combination already does something: Ctrl+G groups, Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups, and Shift+G belongs to another shortcut. `it.each` reports each combination separately, so you can see which check broke.
- **Gap:** the `Keyboard` helper can't hold ⌘ (Cmd), so the `metaKey` check isn't tested.

### 3e. Ctrl+G still groups

```tsx
it("should still group elements with Ctrl+G", () => {
  const rect1 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0 });
  const rect2 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 100 });
  API.setElements([rect1, rect2]);
  act(() => {
    API.setSelectedElements([rect1, rect2]);
  });

  Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
  });

  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
  expect(h.elements[0].groupIds).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(h.elements[0].groupIds).toEqual(h.elements[1].groupIds);
});
```

- **Why:** 3d only checks that the panel stays closed. This test checks that grouping still works. The new handler calls `event.stopPropagation()` and `return`, so a mistake there could block grouping completely. The regression tests do cover Ctrl+G, but only inside long snapshot scenarios. This test checks it on its own.

### 3f. G does nothing in view mode

```tsx
it("should not open the panel in view mode", () => {
  API.setAppState({ viewModeEnabled: true });
  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** pressing G in view mode shouldn't even quietly set the open flag.
- **Limit:** the panel is also hidden in view mode (2h). So this test can't tell whether the key handler skipped G or the panel was simply hidden. To be stricter, also assert `editorJotaiStore.get(isGridPanelOpenAtom)` is `false`.

The rule there is that a host app passing `gridModeEnabled` controls the grid itself, so the editor doesn't show its own grid toggle. These tests apply that rule to the new places a toggle appears.

```tsx

  const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
  expect(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")).toBe(null);

  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
  expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
  expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(gridModeEnabled);
});
```

- **Why:** these cover the `isActionEnabled(actionToggleGridMode)` check in the Toolbar, the panel and the G handler. In the first test, the `toolbar-frame` line makes sure the menu actually opened. Otherwise "Grid not found" would also pass if the menu never opened.
- **Limit of the second test:** I originally asserted that the grid stays on. That failed, because `<Excalidraw gridModeEnabled={true} />` leaves the grid off after load, and this was already the case before your branch. So the test now only checks that G changes nothing. ## 5. Preferences ([L284-L330](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx#L284-L330))

These cover change #6. No test opened the Preferences submenu before.

```tsx
const openPreferences = (container: HTMLElement) => {
  fireEvent.click(container.querySelector(".dropdown-menu-button")!);
  const trigger = queryByText(
    document.querySelector(".dropdown-menu") as HTMLElement,
    "Preferences",
  )!.closest("[role='menuitem']")!;
  fireEvent.keyDown(trigger, { key: "ArrowRight" });
  return document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
    ".excalidraw-main-menu-preferences-submenu",
  )!;
};
```

This opens the main menu and then presses → (ArrowRight) on "Preferences". That's the keyboard way to open a submenu, and it works in the test environment, unlike hovering. One thing I found: `<Excalidraw />` with no children has **no** Preferences entry. Only the excalidraw.com app adds one, in [AppMainMenu.tsx:79](excalidraw-app/components/AppMainMenu.tsx#L79). So both tests render it explicitly.

### 5a. The default list no longer has the grid toggles

```tsx
it("should no longer list the grid toggles by default", async () => {
  const { container } = await render(
    <Excalidraw>
      <MainMenu>
        <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences />
      </MainMenu>
    </Excalidraw>,
  );
  const submenu = openPreferences(container);

  expect(submenu).not.toBe(null);
  // sanity check that the submenu contents rendered
  expect(queryByText(submenu, "Zen mode")).not.toBe(null);
  expect(queryByText(submenu, "Toggle grid")).toBe(null);
  expect(queryByText(submenu, "Snap to grid")).toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** this pins down the two lines removed from [DefaultItems.tsx:638](packages/excalidraw/components/main-menu/DefaultItems.tsx#L638). The "Zen mode" check proves the submenu really opened. Without it, "grid items not found" would also pass when the submenu never rendered.

### 5b. Host apps can still add them

```tsx
it("should still allow hosts to add the grid toggles explicitly", async () => {
  const { container } = await render(
    <Excalidraw>
      <MainMenu>
        <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences>
          <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.ToggleGridMode />
          <MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.ToggleGridSnapMode />
        </MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences>
      </MainMenu>
    </Excalidraw>,
  );
  const submenu = openPreferences(container);

  expect(queryByText(submenu, "Toggle grid")).not.toBe(null);
  expect(queryByText(submenu, "Snap to grid")).not.toBe(null);
});
```

- **Why:** `Preferences.ToggleGridMode` and `Preferences.ToggleGridSnapMode` are public parts of the npm package. Removing them from the default list must not delete them or break them for apps that use them. Without this test, someone tidying up could delete the "unused" components.

```text
export const PreferencesToggleGridModeItem = () => {
  const { t } = useI18n();
  const actionManager = useExcalidrawActionManager();
  const appState = useUIAppState();

  return (
    <DropdownMenuItemCheckbox
      checked={appState.gridModeEnabled}
      shortcut={getShortcutFromShortcutName("gridMode")}
      onSelect={(event) => {
        actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleGridMode);
        event.preventDefault();
      }}
    >
      {t("labels.toggleGrid")}
    </DropdownMenuItemCheckbox>
  );
};
```
